surfaces: Layers of meaning card (web/src/ui/Layers.tsx LayersCard, in the Links panel, every level including Simple). It starts closed: the heading, one line and the button 'Read the notes'. The notice opens when that button is tapped. On a wide screen the card is on every first visit (Isaiah 53:5), so it can never open by itself.

Wordplay and name notes, verse panel only (extras/wordplay.extra.tsx, every level; the panel shows Layers notes word for word). The notice opens when the reader taps the 'A play on words: ...' or 'What a name means: ...' line, before the panel opens. The alphabet-poem chapter panel stays open.
Study notes (extras/notes.extra.tsx, Study). The notice opens when the reader taps the 'A study note on ...' line.
Often asked (extras/hard-verses.extra.tsx, Study). The notice opens when the reader taps the 'Often asked: ...' line. No card is live today; this covers the first approved one.
Old Bible dictionaries under a verse (extras/dictionary.extra.tsx, Study). The notice opens when the reader taps the 'In old Bible dictionaries: ...' line.

An old dictionary entry on the Sources shelf (web/src/ui/Dictionary.tsx). Search and the list of names stay open. An opened entry shows one line and 'Show the entry', and that button opens the notice.
Christian writers (extras/voices.extra.tsx, Deep). The notice opens when the reader taps the 'Christian writers: ...' line. It replaces the old one-click 'Show what they wrote' opt-in (atlas.voices).

Hard passages (extras/hard-passages.extra.tsx, Deep). The panel opens as it does today, with the passages side by side, because Scripture is never gated. Only the list of answers on other websites is closed, behind 'Show the answers', and that button opens the notice.
Dating views behind the When/Written line (web/src/ui/ChapterWhen.tsx, every level). The line itself stays. Tapping 'More' opens the notice first.
A panel opened by a shared link, or brought back by Back or Forward, opens in its closed state: one line and a button. The notice waits for that button and never opens on arrival.

Never gated, and never open the notice: the BSB, NET and ESV text, the original words, the word study (including LSJ and UBS), cross-references, quotations, parallels, places, themes, paths, Ask the Bible and its chains, the Peshitta, Aramaic notes, Nave's rows, the Sources shelf cards, and the lines under a verse themselves.
design.words:
PAGE 1 OF 2. Heading: "This is commentary, not God’s Word". Two boxes: "The Bible / God’s Word" and "Commentary / People’s words about the Bible". Text: "What you are about to read was written by people. It can help you understand the Bible, but it is not the Bible." Button: "Next ›". Top right: "Not now".

PAGE 2 OF 2. Heading: "Check it with the Bible". Text: "Test what you read against the Bible, as the people of Berea did:". Verse, copied from the repo's BSB data (web/public/data/bsb.txt line 27535; data/raw/examples.bsb@48a9feb71f/45ACTBSB.usfm line 1083 under \c 17): “Now the Bereans were more noble-minded than the Thessalonians, for they received the message with great eagerness and examined the Scriptures every day to see if these teachings were true.” Under it: "Acts 17:11, Berean Standard Bible". Text: "If anything here disagrees with the Bible, trust the Bible." Buttons: "‹ Back" and "I understand. Show the commentary". Top right: "Not now".

SEEING IT AGAIN: "Close" replaces "Not now", and "I understand" replaces "I understand. Show the commentary".

CLOSED STATES (one line, then a button):
- Layers: "Notes on what this passage means, drawn from Christian writers." / Read the notes
- Christian writers: "The Church Fathers, Matthew Henry and John Wesley wrote about John 3:16." / Show what they wrote
- Study notes: "Bible scholars wrote a note on this verse." / Show the note (or Show the notes)
- Dictionaries: "An entry in an old Bible dictionary names Exodus 16:13." / Show the entry (or Show the entries)
- Often asked: "People often ask: How did Judas die?" / Show the answer
- Wordplay: "Writers note a play on words here." / Show the note
- Hard passages: "Other websites answer the questions this passage raises." / Show the answers
- Shelf entry: "This entry is from Easton’s Bible Dictionary, 1897." / Show the entry

AFTER FINISHING, at the end of each commentary surface: "Commentary, not God’s Word · See the notice again".

SOURCES SHELF SECTION. Heading: "Commentary". Text: "Some parts of this app show commentary: people’s words about the Bible, not God’s Word. They open after a short notice." Once finished: "Commentary is open on this device." with "See the notice again" and "Close commentary again". Before finishing: "See the notice".
decisions: The words: please confirm both pages and the closed-state lines exactly as written. In particular, page 2 ends with 'If anything here disagrees with the Bible, trust the Bible.'
The verse: Acts 17:11 in full, from the BSB. A shorter option is 1 Thessalonians 5:21 ('but test all things. Hold fast to what is good.'), but it starts in the middle of a sentence.

Where the line falls. Behind the notice: Layers, wordplay notes, study notes, Often asked, the old dictionaries, Christian writers, the answers linked from Hard passages, and the dating views behind 'More'. Left open as borderline: Aramaic notes, word meanings, 'Outside the Bible' (LSJ), 'In their world' (UBS), and the short 'Written: ...' line itself.
The first screen changes. The Layers card on Isaiah 53:5, which every first visit sees on a wide screen, now starts closed for everyone until they finish the notice.

Christian writers fold-in. The notice replaces the one-click 'Show what they wrote' opt-in. Readers who had already opted in (atlas.voices) see the notice once. 'Hide writers’ notes' becomes 'Close commentary again' on the Sources shelf, and it closes all commentary, not only the writers.

Leaving the notice. Escape and a click outside do nothing, as you asked. Phone Back counts as 'Not now': the notice closes and the commentary stays closed. With storage blocked, the notice shows once per visit.

Building it needs three small changes to the extras spine files: types.ts gains a commentary flag, VerseExtras/open.ts waits for the notice before opening a panel, and Sheet.tsx skips its Escape handler while the notice is open. This was done on purpose before, in #17, #22 and #27.

Note: the message that started this run ('make the puritan thing cite something that translates it correctly where readers would get confused') looks like a different task. It seems to be about older writers' wording and citing a faithful plain-English rendering. This spec does not cover it.
